title: National Clinical Care Commission Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the Senate on September 6, 2017. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

National Clinical Care Commission Act

(Sec. 2) This bill establishes within the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) a National Clinical Care Commission to evaluate and make recommendations regarding improvements to the coordination and leveraging of federal programs related to complex metabolic or autoimmune diseases that result from issues related to insulin and represent a significant disease burden (e.g., diabetes). The commission must report on: (1) HHS programs that focus on prevention, (2) current activities and gaps in federal efforts to support clinicians in providing integrated care, (3) improvement in federal education and awareness activities related to prevention and treatment, (4) methods for outreach and dissemination of education and awareness materials, and (5) opportunities for consolidation of overlapping federal programs.

The commission must submit an operating plan to HHS and Congress within 90 days of its first meeting. The commission is terminated after it submits a final report, but not later than the end of FY2021.

summary.headline: This law creates a temporary federal commission to review and recommend better coordination of programs for diseases tied to insulin, such as diabetes.
summary.what_it_does: It sets up a National Clinical Care Commission inside the Department of Health and Human Services. The commission must study federal prevention programs, gaps in support for clinicians who provide integrated care, federal education and awareness efforts, and ways to share educational materials. It must also look for overlapping federal programs that could be combined, and it must submit an operating plan within 90 days of its first meeting.

who_it_affects.group: People with diabetes and other insulin-related diseases
who_it_affects.how: The commission may recommend changes to federal prevention, education, and treatment efforts that serve them.

who_it_affects.group: Clinicians who treat patients with complex metabolic or autoimmune diseases
who_it_affects.how: The commission must examine federal gaps in support for providing integrated care and may recommend changes.

who_it_affects.group: Department of Health and Human Services and other federal program offices
who_it_affects.how: They must work with the commission and may see their programs reviewed for overlap or consolidation.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on November 2, 2017. The commission ends after it submits its final report, and no later than the end of fiscal year 2021.
